Subject: Quick follow-up: deployment isolation needs (PHI/clinical data)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Helpful overview. I wanted to capture our key must-haves so we can move toward procurement:

- We will be sending PHI and clinical trial data to the inference endpoint (redacted identifiers + payloads).
- Our security/risk team requires firm assurances that: no customer plaintext is written to shared disks accessible to other tenants, KV caches are isolated per-tenant, and network egress can be restricted to our managed VPC endpoints.
- Preference: Private VPC (customer-managed networking) if it meets the above. Dedicated capacity is acceptable if we can get the same guarantees for data-at-rest and KV/cache tenancy.

Can you provide an itemized acceptance criteria checklist (network controls, KMS/HSM boundaries, audit log retention, evidence artifacts you can provide) and a sample network diagram? Procurement is cc'd and will need the security checklist to progress.

I attached our SOC2 scope summary (see stub) — happy to run through any gap with your security team.

Thanks,
Lisa

Lisa / team —

Following up with a concise technical posture and an acceptance checklist draft. High level: Private VPC provides the clearest boundary (control plane separated, customer-managed network, optional on-prem connectors). Dedicated capacity gives isolated compute but the control plane remains Redwood-managed by default unless you take Private. Key items below.

Draft acceptance criteria (for your security team):
- Data-at-rest: all customer payloads must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMKs) for Private VPC; for Dedicated we support CMKs but some control-plane metadata may be encrypted with Redwood keys unless contractualized. Evidence: KMS config snapshot + key ARNs.
- Disk tenancy: no plaintext persisted on shared host volumes. Ephemeral scratch volumes only; persistent storage for model artifacts isolated per-tenant. Evidence: host-level mount policy + disk encryption cert.
- KV cache segregation: per-tenant KV caches implemented; cache namespace isolated and never swapped between tenants. Evidence: cache tenancy logs + config.
- Network controls: ability to restrict egress to customer-managed NAT or PrivateLink endpoints; firewall/IP allowlist; optional static IPs for outbound. Evidence: network ACLs and VPC peering config diagram.
- Audit & logs: 365-day ingestion of audit logs to customer S3 or a Redacted link; immutable append-only logs for inference requests including request IDs. Evidence: sample logs + retention policy.
- Access controls: RBAC for control-plane actions; MFA for privileged ops; separation of duties for model deployment. Evidence: role matrix + recent access audit.
- Pen test / compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II report, recent pen-test summary (redacted for public delivery), and willingness to coordinate an on-site review for Dedicated/Private procurement.

Open items for OncoForge to confirm:
- Do you require a hardware HSM (FIPS 140-2) for key storage, or is cloud KMS sufficient?
- Is there a required SLA for RTO/RPO on inference endpoints or model reloads?
- Any on-premise air-gap requirements?

If you confirm the HSM + SLA expectations, we can provide a contract appendix that pins the control-plane behaviors and encryption responsibilities. I recommend the technical deep dive so we can walk these artifacts live.

-Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the checklist draft — that aligns with what we need. A few clarifications before the technical deep dive so we can scope attendees: 

- HSM: We would prefer FIPS 140-2 HSM for key custody for production PHI, but for initial pilots (non-production) cloud KMS is acceptable. Please flag any cost or lead-time implications.
- Disk tenancy: to be explicit — no plaintext customer data on any host filesystem backed by multi-tenant storage. Ephemeral scratch only; persistent artifacts must be tenant-scoped.
- KV cache: key requirement is that model KV caches are not accessible across tenants and can be fully flushed on job completion.
- SLA: For production inference targets we need a 99.9% monthly availability SLA and documented RTO for model reloads (max 15 minutes for cache warmup). If Dedicated cannot meet that SLA, we need the Private deployment path.

We can do the technical deep dive on Wed 9/1 10:00am PT — procurement and our cloud infra lead (cc'd separately) will join. Please confirm and send a calendar invite with an agenda and the artifacts you referenced.

Lisa
Director, IT Security
OncoForge Therapeutics
